gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.

gaps.sentence: They ___ a lot of business with companies in Asia.
gaps.explanation: do business with somebody is the fixed expression for commercial activity.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: The thief ran so fast that no one could ___ him.
gaps.hint: to capture someone who is running away
gaps.explanation: catch somebody means to capture or seize them after chasing.

gaps.sentence: I'd like to ___ an appointment to see the manager.
gaps.hint: you arrange an appointment by ___ing it
gaps.explanation: make an appointment is the fixed collocation for arranging a meeting time.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.
